RE-STAMP ONLY, count unmoved at 7. The previous stamp named 7f582912d, which this branch rebased away minutes after banking it: origin/19.0 gained sixteen commits (the GPS fuel-charge series) between the measurement and the push, so the power_user commit was replayed as f411c4e42 and the floor read ORPHANED-BASE. Re-measured on the clean pushed tree -- `py_lint.py agromarin --rule sql-injection --count` reads 7.

Worth naming because the same trap caught two floors in one day: bank a sibling floor AFTER the sibling commit is pushed, not after it is merely committed. A stamp taken at a local tip is a claim about a commit that only exists locally, and any rebase before the push -- including your own, onto a peer's merge -- invalidates it. `lint_noqa_rationale_design-themes` reached the harder UNCHECKED state by exactly this route.

A LOWERING, and the two units it removed were never debt. Both power_user sites are marked `# noqa: E8501` with a written reason: an SQL console behind group_power_manager whose purpose is to execute the statement its user typed, where there is no value to pass as a parameter.

THE PREVIOUS NOTE'S PREMISE WAS FALSE AND IS THE REASON THIS SAT AT 9. It stated, across two revisions, that "_checker_sql honours no noqa, so a deliberate site cannot be marked", and concluded the number could only come down if "the console grows a real parser or the checker grows a suppression with a written reason". The suppression already existed: `sql-injection` is absent from `_rules.UNSUPPRESSABLE`, `_suppression.comment_suppresses` applies to it as to every other suppressible rule, and `_rules.RULES` has always advertised `add `# noqa: E8501  <why this one is safe>`` in the rule's own guidance. Measured before changing anything: a single probe noqa on line 124 took the count 9 -> 8.

So a floor absorbed two intentional constructs for as long as a note asserted the door was locked. That is the failure mode §4 names for CHECK-constraint shapes -- a rule reading the syntax alone banks a correct construct as debt -- arriving by a different route: not the rule's blindness, but a claim about the rule that nobody re-tested.

Re-measure with `py_lint.py agromarin --rule sql-injection --count`. If this rises again, read the new site before banking: seven of the nine counted units were the same console shape, and a genuine finding in this repository would look nothing like them.

A RAISE, AND THE ONLY ONE IN THIS PASS. Both new sites are power_user/models/power_user_sql.py -- an admin SQL console gated behind group_power_manager, whose entire purpose is to run a statement the user typed. Line 124 DECLAREs a cursor FOR that statement and line 147 executes it plainly when DECLARE refuses it. Neither can be written so the checker stops seeing it without lying about what the module does, and _checker_sql honours no noqa, so there is no way to mark a deliberate site. They arrived with the paged-cursor feature (d3f88a630, 8ff38db32, a9fef92d3), after the floor was stamped at d2054a34a. The other seven counted sites are the same shape in the same tree.
